questions.stem: What does « l'estime de soi » mean?
questions.explanation: « L'estime de soi » is how much a person values themselves, a key term for adolescence and wellbeing. Selfishness is « l'égoïsme », and self-control is « la maîtrise de soi ».

questions.stem: What does « la pression des pairs » mean?
questions.explanation: « Les pairs » are your equals, people of the same age or status. Parental pressure would be « la pression des parents ».

questions.stem: « Il faut trouver un juste milieu entre le travail et les loisirs. » What must be found?
questions.explanation: « Le juste milieu » is the balance point between two extremes. « Juste » here means 'right' or 'exact', not 'fair' as in a fair wage.

questions.stem: « L'égalité salariale entre les femmes et les hommes n'est pas encore atteinte. » What is being claimed?
options: Women and men were paid equally long ago
Women are now paid more than men
Equal pay is no longer a goal for anyone
Women and men are not yet paid equally
questions.explanation: « Salarial » refers to pay, and « pas encore atteinte » means 'not yet reached'. The « encore » rules out the reading that it has already been achieved.

questions.stem: What does « les droits et les devoirs » mean?
options: the rights and wrongs of an issue
questions.explanation: « Les devoirs » here are duties, the obligations that go with « les droits ». 'Rights and wrongs' would be « le bien et le mal ».

questions.stem: What does « le mal-être des adolescents » refer to?
questions.explanation: « Le mal-être » is the opposite of « le bien-être »: a state of unhappiness or psychological unease. Bad behaviour is « la mauvaise conduite ».

questions.stem: What is « une famille recomposée »?
questions.explanation: A « famille recomposée » is formed when a parent re-partners, bringing step-parents and step-siblings together. A single-parent family is « une famille monoparentale ».

questions.stem: « Léa a des centaines d'“amis” en ligne, mais elle avoue qu'elle se sent souvent seule le week-end. » What is the point?
options: She prefers to be on her own at weekends
She spends her weekends with her online friends
Her online contacts do not stop her feeling lonely
She has few friends online but many offline
questions.explanation: The quotation marks around « amis » cast doubt on these friendships, and « mais » sets them against her loneliness. « Avoue » ('admits') shows that the loneliness is not a preference.

questions.stem: What does « Dans notre famille, on se serre les coudes » mean?
questions.explanation: « Se serrer les coudes » (literally to press elbows together) means to support one another in hard times. It is about solidarity, not physical affection.

questions.stem: « Paul : Tu rentres à quelle heure ce soir ? — Inès : Ben… comme d'hab, quoi. » What does Inès's reply suggest?
options: She will be home at her usual time, without giving one
She will be home earlier than she usually is
She has decided not to go out this evening
She is answering her father in a formal register
questions.explanation: « Comme d'hab » is short for « comme d'habitude », 'as usual', and « ben » and « quoi » are fillers of casual speech. She avoids a precise time, and nothing in the reply is formal.

questions.stem: « J'ai du pain sur la planche cette semaine. » What does the speaker mean?
options: I have hardly any money left
I have a lot of work to do
I have run out of ideas
questions.explanation: « Avoir du pain sur la planche » means having a great deal of work ahead. The bread is figurative.

questions.stem: « Après le bac, Malik hésite : s'inscrire à l'université ou partir un an en Australie pour travailler. Ses parents, eux, préféreraient qu'il commence tout de suite ses études. » What do his parents want?
options: for him to find work in France for a year first
for him to make up his own mind
for him to start university straight away
for him to go and work in Australia
questions.explanation: « Eux » marks a contrast with Malik's hesitation, and « préféreraient qu'il commence tout de suite ses études » states their preference for immediate study. Australia is Malik's alternative, not theirs.

questions.stem: « Le stage ? Ce n'est pas la mer à boire ! » What does the speaker mean?
questions.explanation: « Ce n'est pas la mer à boire » (it isn't like drinking the sea) means the task is not as difficult as it seems. It does not say the effort is wasted.

questions.stem: What does « le chômage des jeunes » mean?
questions.explanation: « Le chômage » is unemployment, and « un chômeur » is an unemployed person. Volunteering is « le bénévolat ».

questions.stem: What does « tomber dans les pommes » mean?
questions.explanation: « Tomber dans les pommes » is an informal idiom for fainting. Falling in love is « tomber amoureux ».

questions.stem: « J'ai la flemme de ranger ma chambre. » How does the speaker feel?
questions.explanation: « Avoir la flemme » is informal for lacking the energy or will to do something. It belongs to casual speech, not to a formal letter.

questions.stem: In a role-play to resolve a disagreement, which phrase acknowledges the other speaker's view?
options: « Je comprends ce que tu veux dire, mais… »
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the other speaker before disagreeing is a negotiation strategy the study design names. The other openings push your own position without recognising theirs.

questions.stem: Which phrase offers a compromise?
options: « Revenons à ce que tu disais. »
« Si je comprends bien, tu refuses tout. »
« Et si on coupait la poire en deux ? »
questions.explanation: « Couper la poire en deux » (to cut the pear in two) means to split the difference. « Revenons à ce que tu disais » links back to the other speaker but offers nothing.

questions.stem: Which phrase revisits an unresolved issue?
options: « Je suis tout à fait d'accord. »
« Ça te dirait de venir avec nous ce soir ? »
« Pour revenir à la question de l'argent… »
questions.explanation: « Pour revenir à » brings the discussion back to a point that is still open. « Marché conclu ! » ('it's a deal!') closes an issue rather than reopening it.

questions.stem: Which phrase confirms the outcome at the end of a negotiation?
options: « Alors, c'est entendu : je rentre à minuit. »
« Je vois ce que tu veux dire. »
« Ça dépend de toi, en fait. »
questions.explanation: « C'est entendu » means 'that's agreed', and restating the deal checks both speakers understand it. « Je vois ce que tu veux dire » acknowledges a view but settles nothing.

questions.stem: Which phrase checks that you have understood the other speaker?
options: « J'en ai marre de tout ça. »
« Si je comprends bien, tu veux… »
« Peu importe ce que tu veux. »
questions.explanation: « Si je comprends bien » introduces a summary of the other person's position for them to confirm. It is a clarifying strategy that keeps a negotiation on track.

questions.stem: In a role-play, your host father has refused to lend you his car. Which reply links to his concern and persuades politely?
options: « Tu dois me prêter ta voiture, c'est tout. »
« Je comprends que tu t'inquiètes, alors je prends la voiture. »
« Vous avez tort, je conduis très bien. »
« Je comprends que vous vous inquiétiez, mais je vous promets d'être prudent. »
questions.explanation: It acknowledges his worry, answers it with a promise, and keeps « vous » for an adult host. The reply with « tu » ignores his refusal, and « vous avez tort » contradicts him without offering anything.

questions.stem: Negotiating hours with an employer, why say « Serait-il possible de finir à 17 h ? » rather than « Je veux finir à 17 h »?
options: The conditional is required whenever « possible » is used
« Je veux » is ungrammatical before an infinitive
Questions in French must always use inversion
The conditional softens the request to suit a formal relationship
questions.explanation: The conditional makes a request tentative and polite, which matters when speaking to someone of higher status. « Je veux » plus an infinitive is perfectly grammatical; it is simply too blunt here.

questions.stem: From a magazine: « Selon une enquête, près d'un lycéen sur deux dit dormir moins de sept heures par nuit en période d'examens. » What does the survey report?
options: Half of the students sleep more than seven hours at exam time
One student in seven sleeps badly at exam time
Most students sleep about seven hours all year round
Nearly half of the students sleep under seven hours at exam time
questions.explanation: « Près d'un sur deux » is 'nearly one in two', and « moins de sept heures » is 'under seven hours'. The finding is limited to « en période d'examens ».

questions.stem: From a blog: « Pendant longtemps, j'ai cru que réussir, c'était gagner beaucoup d'argent. Aujourd'hui, je pense plutôt que c'est avoir le temps de vivre. » How has the writer's view changed?
options: from success as wealth to success as having time to live
from success as having time to success as wealth
from wanting success to rejecting the idea of success
from earning little money to earning a great deal
questions.explanation: The imperfect « c'était » gives the old belief and « aujourd'hui… plutôt » the new one. The writer redefines success; they do not reject it.

questions.stem: « Ma grand-mère n'a jamais compris pourquoi je passe des heures devant un écran. Pourtant, c'est elle qui m'envoie maintenant des messages vocaux tous les matins ! » What is the tone of the last sentence?
questions.explanation: « Pourtant » and the exclamation set the grandmother's new habit against her old disapproval, which is gently ironic. Nothing suggests the writer is upset by it.

questions.stem: « Les jeunes d'aujourd'hui ne savent plus ce que c'est que l'effort ! » What attitude does the speaker show?
questions.explanation: « Ne… plus » ('no longer') implies young people have lost something earlier generations had. It is a classic generational complaint, not sympathy.

questions.stem: « Ce qui compte pour moi, ce n'est pas le salaire, mais de faire un métier qui ait du sens. » What does the speaker value most in a career?
options: a job with plenty of free time
questions.explanation: « Ce n'est pas… mais » rejects salary and puts meaning first. The subjunctive « ait » after « un métier qui » shows the job is wished for, not yet found.

questions.stem: What does « l'épanouissement personnel » mean?
questions.explanation: « S'épanouir » means to blossom or flourish, so « l'épanouissement » is fulfilment. It is a common goal in discussions of careers and wellbeing.

questions.stem: What does « Il a du mal à se faire des amis » mean?
options: He makes friends with bad people
He has trouble keeping in touch
He finds it hard to make friends
questions.explanation: « Avoir du mal à » plus an infinitive means to find something difficult. « Se faire des amis » is to make friends.

questions.stem: In an article on gender equality, what is « la charge mentale »?
options: the mental load of organising the household
the stress of final exams at the end of secondary school
the cost of mental health care
the pressure of a demanding job
questions.explanation: « La charge mentale » is the invisible work of planning and remembering domestic tasks, often carried mainly by women. It is a key term in French debates on equality at home.

questions.stem: What does « les stéréotypes de genre » mean?
questions.explanation: « Le genre » here means gender, as in « l'égalité des genres ». In other contexts, « un genre » is a type or a literary genre.

questions.stem: What does « Mon père et moi, on ne voit pas les choses du même œil » mean?
options: My father and I see things differently
My father and I have the same eyes
My father and I never look at each other
My father and I agree on everything
questions.explanation: « Voir les choses du même œil » is to share a view, so the negative means to see things differently. The idiom is useful when describing generational differences.

questions.stem: What does « vivre en colocation » mean?
options: to live in a university college
to share a flat with others
questions.explanation: « La colocation » is flat-sharing, and a flatmate is « un colocataire » or informally « un coloc ». Living alone is « vivre seul ».

questions.stem: « À dix-huit ans, Chloé a quitté le nid familial : elle a pris son envol. » What does « elle a pris son envol » mean here?
questions.explanation: « Prendre son envol » (to take flight) follows the image of « le nid familial », the family nest: Chloé has left home to stand on her own feet. Nothing suggests she ran away.

questions.stem: « Après le bac, Théo fait un BTS en alternance. » What does « en alternance » mean?
options: combining study with paid work in a company
studying at two different universities at the same time
questions.explanation: « L'alternance » is a work-study arrangement in which students alternate between classes and a placement with an employer. Repeating a year is « redoubler ».

questions.stem: What is « une reconversion professionnelle »?
questions.explanation: « Se reconvertir » is to retrain for a new career, often in mid-life. A promotion is « une promotion » and retirement « la retraite ».

questions.stem: « Pour Sarah, réussir sa vie ne passe pas forcément par de longues études ; elle préfère apprendre un métier manuel et créer sa propre entreprise. » What does Sarah think?
options: Long study isn't needed; she prefers a trade and her own business
Long studies are the only path to success, so she will go to university
Manual trades are poorly paid, so she would rather work for a large company
Starting a business is too risky, so she plans to study for many years
questions.explanation: « Ne passe pas forcément par » means 'does not necessarily go through', so she rejects the idea that success requires long study. « Préfère » introduces her chosen path.

questions.stem: What does « Mon frère cadet me tape sur les nerfs » mean?
options: My older brother is very nervous
My younger brother gets on my nerves
My older brother hits me whenever he is angry
My younger brother calms my nerves
questions.explanation: « Taper sur les nerfs » is an informal idiom for irritating someone, and « cadet » means younger; older is « aîné ».

questions.stem: « Il passe son temps à liker les photos de ses amis au lieu de leur parler. » What attitude does the writer show?
options: concern that he has no friends to talk to at all
approval of social media as a way to make friends
criticism that likes replace real conversation
admiration for how well he keeps in touch with friends
questions.explanation: « Au lieu de leur parler » ('instead of talking to them') sets the online habit against real contact, and « passe son temps » suggests excess. The friends exist; the complaint is about how he relates to them.

questions.stem: What does « se confier à quelqu'un » mean?
questions.explanation: « Se confier à » is to share personal thoughts with someone you trust. Being confident is « avoir confiance en soi ».

questions.stem: What does « l'égalité des chances » mean?
questions.explanation: « Les chances » here are opportunities, not luck. « L'égalité des chances » is the principle that everyone should have the same opportunities in education and work.

questions.stem: « Mon frère est rivé à son portable du matin au soir. » What does « rivé à » mean here?
questions.explanation: « Rivé » means riveted, so « rivé à son portable » pictures someone unable to look away from the phone. « Du matin au soir » adds that it lasts all day.
